counterfactual_missing_items: persistent hypervascular lesions without typical features of hepatocellular carcinoma
alpha-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels within normal ranges
No raw post-resection pathology documenting carcinoma is present; the vignette ends only with a planned elective surgical resection
decisive_items: biopsies at that time showed histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions
response.rationale: R3 is the strongest raw-supported diagnostic candidate: the vignette explicitly documents histologically proven hepatic adenoma without malignancy, and the bleeding spans in R1 explain the acute presentation but are a complication rather than the primary disease. R5 is only a surgical suspicion and is contradicted by the raw 'without typical features of hepatocellular carcinoma' span. C1 is an append-only restatement of R3 using the same histology quote, so it should not be awarded separate champion weight.

rejected.why: The only raw support is a planned suspicion of atypical hepatocellular carcinoma; the vignette explicitly says the lesions were without typical features of HCC, and tumor markers were normal.
C1 merely appends 'histologically proven' to the parent R3 diagnosis using the same raw histology span, so it is a correlated restatement rather than independent added evidence.
